fact: The corrective action request is numbered KC-CAR-24-088 on form KC-QF-131 revision D, and was opened on 17.09.2024.
The CAR was raised by B. Aaltonen of Quality, with J. Lindqvist, Head of Ops Gdynia, as action owner.
The source of the CAR is Aldermark audit ACA/2024/PL/0319 finding F-01 (major), clause 8.9.4.2, with priority ticked HIGH.
The problem described is a dairy load for Oakhaven with a 9 h excursion on 14.06.2024 on the GDY-1 yard row.
The release for delivery was signed on KC-QF-114 by the shift lead only on 16.06.2024 at 04:40, without evaluation by the Food Safety Team Leader.
The immediate correction was done on 17.09.2024 at 14:00 as a Tidewalk broadcast to all 38 shift leads.
The broadcast ordered that for any excursion over 4 h the shift lead must call B. Aaltonen on mobile, 24 h, before any release.

Why 2 of the 5-why analysis: the authority matrix in PRO-017 rev C names the shift lead as sufficient for customer-released loads.
Why 3: the FSTL could not be reached by the owls because the on-call number was office hours only.

The root cause is an escalation design gap (authority matrix plus missing on-call), not individual error.

The effectiveness check is planned for 11.11.2024 by B. Aaltonen.

Cargo is classified into six product classes by temperature requirement, entered in Tidewalk in the field "TempClass" and printed on the yard card.
If the shipper's instruction and the class table disagree, the stricter limit applies until the customer confirms the instruction in writing.
Class CH-1 (chilled dairy, ready-to-eat chilled products) has a set point of +1.5 °C, a gate-in product core limit of ≤ +4.5 °C and an air alarm band of set point +2.0 K.
Class CH-2 (fresh fish and seafood, ice packed) has a set point of −0.5 °C, a gate-in product core limit of ≤ +2.0 °C and an air alarm band of set point +1.5 K.
Class CH-3 (berries and soft fruit) has a set point of +0.5 °C, a gate-in product core limit of ≤ +3.0 °C and an air alarm band of set point +2.0 K.
Class CH-4 (citrus and hardy produce) has a set point of +6.5 °C, a gate-in product core limit between +4.0 °C and +9.0 °C and an air alarm band of set point ±2.5 K.
Class FZ-1 (frozen general: meat, bakery, vegetables) has a set point of −20.5 °C, a gate-in product core limit of ≤ −17.5 °C and an air alarm band of set point +3.0 K.
Class FZ-2 (deep-frozen: ice cream, frozen seafood) has a set point of −24.0 °C and a gate-in product core limit of ≤ −21.0 °C.
The CH-4 lower limit exists because of citrus chilling injury and is a contractual limit with Fruttoria Baltica.
Humidity is monitored for CH-3 with a target relative humidity of 90 to 95 per cent but is not a critical limit.
Classes CH-1 and CH-2 have the tightest evaluation rules because vulnerable consumers are possible for dairy, ready-to-eat chilled products and seafood.
The process steps S1 to S14 are shown in flow diagram KC-QF-HACCP-001-F1 and the process was walked at GDY-1 on 19 June 2024, HAM-2 on 26 June 2024 and RTM-3 on 3 July 2024.
A booking without a temperature class is held at status "TEMPCLASS?" until clarified.

The 14 process steps run from S1 booking and pre-advice through gate-in, product temperature check, PTI, plug-in, yard monitoring, cross-dock transfer, stuffing, gate-out, washing, pest control, water and ice, hygiene and pallets, to S14 rejected and returned cargo.
Hazards are scored for severity (S, 1 to 5) times likelihood (L, 1 to 5); a score of 12 or more is significant and must be controlled by a CCP or OPRP.
Hazards scoring between 6 and 11 are controlled by general prerequisite programmes and reviewed at each team meeting, and those below 6 are recorded only.
The hazard analysis was fully repeated on 11 July 2024 with partial updates on 2 October 2024.

At S2 gate-in, broken seal, tampering or undeclared cargo scores 8 and is controlled by OPRP-4 seals.
Cross-contamination from reused probe thermometers at S3 scores 6 and is controlled by wiping the probe with a 70% isopropanol wipe between containers.
At S4 PTI, a unit unable to hold the set point scores 15 and is controlled by CCP-3, while a refrigerant or oil leak onto cargo scores 4 and is recorded only.

fact: The CCP-1 critical limits are the product core limits of the class table: CH-1 ≤ +4.5 °C, CH-2 ≤ +2.0 °C, CH-3 ≤ +3.0 °C, CH-4 between +4.0 °C and +9.0 °C, FZ-1 ≤ −17.5 °C and FZ-2 ≤ −21.0 °C.
For frozen cargo the CCP-1 surface probe is pressed between two cartons for 3 minutes, and readings are taken after the display has been stable for 30 seconds.
CCP-1 sampling is 3 cartons per container, or 5 cartons when the container holds 21 or more pallet positions, and the highest reading decides.
CCP-1 is checked on every inbound container, recorded on form KC-QF-101 and the Tidewalk gate-in screen, and the paper form is kept 5 years.
If the highest CCP-1 reading exceeds the limit by up to 1.0 K the container is accepted under reservation (AMBER), the customer is called within 2 hours and a yellow card is placed.
If the highest CCP-1 reading exceeds the limit by more than 1.0 K the container is held (RED) and the FSTL or a deputy decides within 4 hours on acceptance, return or quarantine with a sample.
A CH-4 reading below +4.0 °C is treated as amber regardless of the size of the deviation, and the gate clerk alone never gives a refusal.
The FSTL's team reviews 10 per cent of KC-QF-101 forms each month, and probe thermometers are checked every 6 months and calibrated externally every 12 months.
Korvane's power-off trial of 8 February 2023 on a 40 ft high-cube with 22 pallets of dairy at +3 °C ambient gave +1.1 K in the first 40 minutes.
The summer trial at +24 °C ambient gave +2.6 K in 40 minutes.
Revision 10 sets the maximum continuous time without power at 40 minutes for chilled classes CH-1 to CH-4 and 25 minutes for frozen classes FZ-1 and FZ-2.
Revision 9 allowed 45 minutes without power for chilled classes, and the reduction to 40 minutes was agreed by the team on 2 October 2024 after the summer trial results.
Where the truck waited at the gate for a Korvane-caused reason, the CCP-2 time starts at the gate-in timestamp.

PTI technicians take training course PTI-110 with 18 months validity, and a PTI is mandatory for Korvane-supplied containers, units with a fault alarm, and units idle more than 14 days.

The cold dock at GDY-1 is kept at +8 °C and the docks at HAM-2 and RTM-3 at +10 °C by design.
The CCP-4 dock ambient temperature must not exceed +12.0 °C while a transfer is in progress.
The maximum door-open time per transfer is 12 minutes for chilled classes and 7 minutes for frozen classes.
The cumulative door-open time per container per calendar day must not exceed 25 minutes for chilled or 14 minutes for frozen cargo.
A pallet standing on the dock outside a container for more than 6 minutes (chilled) or 4 minutes (frozen) is exposed and must be core-checked before loading.
Tidewalk warns the dock supervisor when a single door-open event reaches 8 minutes for chilled or 5 minutes for frozen cargo.
The dock supervisor reads the dock thermometer at the start of each transfer wave, recorded on form KC-QF-109, and dock thermometers are checked monthly.
When dock air exceeds +12.0 °C, frozen transfers are suspended until the dock recovers below +10.0 °C, which at HAM-2 takes typically 25 to 35 minutes.
The team reviews the 20 longest door events per site each month and the FSTL signs the monthly summary.
The CCP-5 critical limit is that return-air temperature must not exceed the alarm band for more than 30 consecutive minutes in chilled classes or 20 consecutive minutes in frozen classes.
Alarms must be acknowledged at the dispatch desk within 10 minutes and someone must be at the container within 25 minutes (15 minutes for frozen classes).

fact: Under revision 9 the shift lead could release any load the customer declared customer-released, and that clause was deleted in revision 10 under corrective action KC-CAR-24-088 with PRO-017 revision D.
The FSTL on-call line has been staffed round the clock since 1 October 2024 on telephone extension 4419.
The FSTL's team reviews every KC-QF-114 form within 5 working days, and an unannounced night test call to the on-call line is made twice a year with a 10-minute answer target.
Empty containers are washed after CH-2 or FZ-2 cargo, when soiled, odorous or leaked, and at the latest every 10 trips for a Korvane-supplied container.
Washing follows work instruction WI-WASH-02 at the GDY-1 and RTM-3 washing bays, while HAM-2 sends containers to the Waltershof wash contractor, audited annually.
The wash uses alkaline detergent KC-Clean Alkaline 40 at 2.5 per cent (v/v) and 55 °C with a contact time of 10 minutes, then rinse until rinse-water pH is between 6.5 and 8.0.
Disinfection uses a peracetic acid sanitiser at 150 ppm with 5 minutes contact, followed by drying for at least 20 minutes with the door open.
Washing is verified by ATP swabs at 3 points with a result below 150 RLU, and one container in every 25 washed is swabbed.
Monthly microbiological swabs have acceptance values of total aerobic count below 100 CFU per 25 cm² and Listeria absent, and records on form KC-QF-122 are kept 3 years.

The notice dated 14 March 2024 is from the Port of Gdynia Authority Compliance Desk and applies from 1 July 2024 unless stated otherwise.
The notice is based on Harbour Master's Order no. 14/2023 (port regulations of 19 December 2023, section 6) and the Port Environmental Committee decision of 29 February 2024.
The notice replaces the earlier circular ZMPG/OS/2022/0088 of 6 June 2022.

Fixed refrigeration units with 3 kg or more of fluorinated refrigerant, including units on containers on a tenant's premises for more than 72 hours, must be entered in the Port Environmental Register by 30 June 2024.
The registration fee is 190 PLN per site per year, and each entry states serial number, refrigerant designation, nominal charge in kg, date of last leak check and responsible person.
A logbook for each registered unit must stay at the unit's site and be retained for 5 years.
Leak checks are once every 12 months for charges from 3 kg up to 29 kg, every 6 months for 30 kg up to 299 kg, and every 3 months for 300 kg and above.
Leak checkers need a refrigerant handling certificate of category I or II, leaks must be repaired within 14 days and rechecked within 30 days after repair.
The annual leakage rate of a tenant's total registered charge must not exceed 5 per cent, otherwise a remediation plan is due within 45 days of year end.

Electrical pedestals for refrigerated containers must be inspected at least every 12 months including a thermographic scan under at least 70 per cent of rated current, and pedestals with a surface rise of more than 40 K above ambient go out of use.
The sound limit at the tenant boundary is 60 dB(A) from 06:00 to 22:00 and 50 dB(A) from 22:00 to 06:00.
The port's noise campaign runs from 8 to 12 April 2024, and tenants exceeding a limit by more than 3 dB(A) must submit a noise reduction plan within 30 days of the result.
Spills of more than 20 litres of fuel or oil and releases of 2 kg or more of refrigerant must be reported to port control by telephone within 4 hours and in writing within 3 working days.

Inspectors may inspect yards without notice from 15 April 2024, fines are 2,000 PLN to 25,000 PLN per breach and doubled for repeat breaches within 12 months, and appeals go to the Harbour Master within 14 days.
